Pepper Money Increases Concessionary Purchase LTV to 85%
summary:
Pepper Money has increased the maximum loan-to-value (LTV) available on concessionary purchases from 75% to 85% of the property’s full market value, giving eligible customers greater flexibility when buying a property at a discounted price from a close family member, or buying the home they currently rent from their landlord. 
 
The change reduces the seller discount needed for eligible purchases from 25% to 15%, where the buyer borrows the full discounted purchase price. Under a concessionary purchase, the difference between the property’s full market value and the discounted purchase price can act as the buyer’s deposit. Eligible customers can borrow up to 100% of the discounted purchase price, including fees, subject to a maximum of 85% of the property’s full market value and applicable lending criteria. 
 
For example, where an eligible buyer borrows the full discounted purchase price without contributing a cash deposit, assuming fees are paid separately, a property with a £300,000 market value would require a seller discount of £45,000 (15%) at 85% LTV, compared with £75,000 (25%) at the previous 75% maximum. The maximum loan in that example rises from £225,000 to £255,000, subject to affordability and lending criteria. 
 
The change could help existing tenants buy from their landlord, or relatives buy from a close family member. 
Paul Adams, Director of Sales at Pepper Money, said: “A close family member or landlord may be willing to sell at a discount, but a 25% reduction can be a significant concession. Increasing our maximum LTV to 85% means eligible buyers borrowing the full discounted purchase price can proceed with a smaller concession from the seller. 
 
“For brokers, it provides another option when helping customers whose circumstances do not fit a conventional purchase.” 
The new 85% LTV maximum is available now, subject to Pepper Money’s usual affordability, credit and lending requirements.

title: Broadridge Appoints Ervin Zaljević as Director of Regulatory Solutions in Luxembourg
summary:
Broadridge today announced the appointment of Ervin Zaljević as Director, Regulatory Solutions, based in Luxembourg. In this role, Ervin will strengthen Broadridge's engagement with Luxembourg's investment funds and asset management community, bringing local market expertise to the company's global regulatory and technology capabilities.
 
Ervin will focus on strengthening relationships across the local funds ecosystem, combining regulatory expertise, market intelligence, industry engagement and strategic client support. His appointment reflects Broadridge's continued engagement with Luxembourg, a leading international investment fund centre, and its commitment to supporting clients navigating an increasingly complex regulatory environment.
“I'm delighted to join Broadridge and bring my experience across asset management, fund servicing and legal practice to its work with Luxembourg's financial services community,” said Ervin. “I look forward to connecting local market insights with Broadridge's global capabilities to help clients navigate regulatory complexity, strengthen operational efficiency and respond to change. I also look forward to contributing to industry dialogue and knowledge sharing across Luxembourg's funds ecosystem.”
“Luxembourg plays an important role in the global funds industry, and understanding the market’s regulatory environment and evolving client needs is essential to serving it effectively,” said Stephen Johnston, head of Broadridge’s Regulatory Communications EU/UK business. “Ervin brings a valuable combination of legal, fund servicing and regulatory expertise that will deepen our engagement with the local industry and help us connect clients with Broadridge’s global capabilities as the market continues to evolve.”
Ervin previously served as Head of Legal at BlackRock Luxembourg and as a board member of numerous investment funds and corporate entities. He also headed up the Fund Corporate Services team at RBC Investor Services Bank and practised as a corporate and investment funds lawyer at leading Luxembourg law firms. His background brings together legal, governance and fund servicing experience, alongside a deep understanding of Luxembourg's investment funds ecosystem.

title: Chelsea FC Announces Multi-Year Sleeve Partnership With Sokin, the Business Payments and FX Platform
summary:
Chelsea Football Club has today announced a multi-year partnership with Sokin, the embedded finance and payments company used by businesses worldwide. Sokin will be named a Principal Partner and Official Business Payments and FX Partner of Chelsea FC and Chelsea FC Women.
As a Principal Partner, Sokin will be represented on the sleeves of the Chelsea FC men’s, women’s and academy home, away, and third kits from the 2026/27 season.
The partnership brings together two ambitious London-headquartered organisations with worldwide reach – a club with millions of fans across the world and a fintech platform through which businesses move more than $11 billion a year. A club of Chelsea’s scale works in many currencies every day, with partners, competitions and supporters around the world, and needs a financial partner built to handle that.
Sokin gives finance teams business payments, multi-currency accounts, foreign exchange, checkout and treasury in one place, so they spend less time juggling banks and providers and keep more of what they move.
As Official Business Payments and FX Partner, Sokin will simplify how Chelsea FC sends, receives and manages money in the currencies the club operates in.
The Sokin logo featured on the sleeve of the Chelsea shirt for the first time when the men’s team host Tottenham Hotspur at Stamford Bridge on Saturday 24th October.
Jason Gannon, President at Chelsea FC said: “At Chelsea, we seek to partner with organisations that share our ambition and innovative mindset. Sokin’s expertise in business payments, and their focus on making both simpler for the businesses they serve, makes them a natural fit for the Club. We are pleased to welcome Sokin to the Chelsea family and look forward to working together in the years ahead.”
‍Vroon Modgill, CEO and founder at Sokin said: “Chelsea plays on the biggest stage in world football, and its business runs in dozens of currencies. Sokin was built for that with regulated, multi-currency payments and foreign exchange for organisations that operate internationally. We’re proud to be the platform behind the business payments and FX of one of the most iconic teams in football. Sokin’s platform serves businesses in more than 170 countries. We’re thrilled to be partners for the season ahead. An organisation as sophisticated as Chelsea doesn’t leave its finances to chance.”

Vancity Selects Temenos SaaS to Modernize Core Banking
summary:
Temenos, a global leader in banking technology, today announced that Vancity has selected Temenos SaaS to modernize its core banking platform and support its next phase of growth.
Serving the needs of more than 588,000 members across more than three million accounts and reporting CAD $42.4 billion in assets, Vancity is Canada’s largest credit union and one of the country’s most significant member-owned financial institutions.
With Temenos, Vancity will follow a build-and-migrate strategy, enabling it to introduce new digital banking capabilities while progressively modernizing its existing operations. This approach will help Vancity transition to Temenos’ modern SaaS platform at a pace that protects members, operations and business continuity.
The transformation program will support core banking operations across Vancity’s main business lines, including retail deposits, retail lending, corporate banking, and payments. The scope includes Temenos Core, Temenos Payments Hub and Temenos Data Hub.
Deployed on Microsoft Azure, Temenos SaaS will provide Vancity with a scalable and resilient foundation while simplifying the management of its core banking technology and supporting its ESG commitments through a more efficient technology environment.
Wendy Murphy, Chief Technology Officer, Vancity, commented: “Banking is changing, and the technology behind it needs to change too. Moving to Temenos SaaS represents a deliberate shift toward a simpler, more scalable technology foundation that can continuously evolve, allowing Vancity to innovate faster and respond to our members’ changing needs. It means we can spend less time managing complexity and more time investing in better banking experiences for our members.”
Brian DuVal, President, North America, Temenos, said: “Vancity is one of Canada’s most significant financial institutions with a broad and sophisticated banking operation. This program underscores how Temenos’ modern technology platform can help established financial institutions across North America move core banking operations to the cloud while supporting the breadth and complexity of their business.”

Nasdaq Strengthens Asia-Pacific Leadership Team
summary:
Nasdaq today announced the appointment of Andrew Murray as Senior Vice President, Financial Technology, Asia-Pacific, strengthening its senior presence in one of the world’s most dynamic regions. Based in Singapore, Murray will deepen Nasdaq’s Financial Technology client partnerships and accelerate business growth across Asia-Pacific, supporting financial institutions as they deliver on their technology and transformation priorities. His appointment follows the relocation to Singapore of Bob McCooey, Vice Chairman and Head of International Listings, a move that enhances Nasdaq’s engagement with the region’s companies and their access to global capital.
These developments position Nasdaq to help advance the region’s technology and capital markets ambitions.
“Asia-Pacific is entering one of the most significant cycles of innovation and market evolution in decades, driven by AI, data and the move toward always-on, globally connected markets,” said Valerie Bannert-Thurner, Executive Vice President and Chief Revenue Officer, Financial Technology at Nasdaq. “Andrew’s strong track record of helping financial institutions solve complex technology challenges will be invaluable as our clients navigate this rapidly changing landscape. Alongside Bob and our teams across the region, we are committed to being a trusted, long-term partner to Asia-Pacific’s market ecosystems.”
Murray brings more than three decades of experience leading teams and building long-term client partnerships at financial technology companies serving treasury, trading, corporate banking and capital markets clients. Most recently, he served as a leader in International Banking and Payments at FIS, where he supported clients across the full banking and payments value chain. His career includes senior international leadership positions at FIS in Banking & Markets and Post-Trade Solutions, as well as previous experience at Calypso Technology (now part of Nasdaq), SunGard, Wall Street Systems and Deutsche Bank.
“Asia-Pacific’s ambition is reshaping the global economy, and the region’s companies and investors increasingly seek access to deep, global pools of capital to fuel that growth,” said Bob McCooey, Vice Chairman and Head of International Listings at Nasdaq. “Strengthening our presence on the ground will allow us to work more closely with the region’s companies, investors and market participants, and deepen our role as a long-term partner across Asia-Pacific. Together, we can bring the full breadth of Nasdaq to support the innovation and economic growth that define this region.”
McCooey’s relocation underscores Nasdaq’s commitment to broadening access to capital and supporting the development of companies and economies across Asia-Pacific. With more than two decades at Nasdaq, McCooey has partnered with many of the region’s most innovative companies on their journeys to the global capital markets. Being based in Singapore will facilitate closer collaboration with clients, partners and local market ecosystems.
Basing two additional senior leaders in Singapore also reflects Nasdaq’s enduring commitment to Asia-Pacific. As the region’s markets become more connected, continuous and technology-driven, Nasdaq will continue to partner with clients, exchanges and market ecosystems to strengthen the trusted infrastructure that supports capital formation and long-term economic growth.

title: TEN Credit Union Selects Bankjoy for Digital Banking as It Moves to Corelation KeyStone
summary:
Bankjoy, a leading provider of digital banking solutions for community financial institutions, today announced that TEN Credit Union (TENCU), a Nashville-based credit union founded in 1950, has selected Bankjoy as its digital banking platform. TENCU will launch Bankjoy the same day it converts to Corelation's KeyStone core, so members will move to a new core and a new digital banking experience in one coordinated conversion.
TENCU members will now have access to Bankjoy's consumer and business digital banking, protected by FraudSense, Bankjoy's real-time, multi-layered fraud prevention platform. The launch also includes advanced card controls through a tight integration with Velera. JoyCompass, Bankjoy's financial wellness platform, and Plaid-powered account verification and aggregation are part of the agreement and can be turned on after launch.
Bankjoy connects directly to KeyStone through Corelation's KeyBridge API and was the first fintech certified through Corelation's vendor certification program. That direct integration lets TENCU run its digital banking on its new core from the first day, with no second digital conversion to plan afterward.
“A core conversion is the most important project a credit union can undertake. Our members trust us to get this right, and we know digital banking has to be ready on day one. We can’t treat it as an afterthought,” said Michael Roussel, Chief Innovation Officer. “Bankjoy has proven to work seamlessly with KeyStone, and we’re confident they’ll not only be an awesome partner to TENCU, but they will deliver the best experience for our members."
“TENCU has served Tennessee educators and their communities for more than 75 years, and we're honored they chose Bankjoy for their next chapter,” said Michael Duncan, CEO of Bankjoy. “Credit unions moving to KeyStone want a digital partner that already knows the core and has launched on it many times. That experience is what we bring to TENCU, along with real-time fraud protection and tools that help members do more with their money.”
TENCU joins a growing group of credit unions that pair Bankjoy with KeyStone. The credit unions that are using Bankjoy with Corelation's KeyStone core, are seeing measurable gains in member engagement. At CommunityWide Federal Credit Union, 91.8% of members who created a budget in JoyCompass remained active in digital banking after three months, compared with 66.4% of members who did not use Spending Analysis. More credit unions are also choosing KeyStone: Corelation reported earlier this month that six credit unions with more than $5.4 billion in combined assets selected the core in the third quarter of 2026.

The partnership leverages Bankjoy's direct integration with the KeyStone core to ensure a seamless transition for members.
